security_review.credentials: Certificates carry synthetic test-only keys and are committed as clearly marked fixture data; the guard never emits or persists private key material beyond the operator-configured listener pair; scope maps are copied defensively at construction and per verdict
security_review.authority: Terminal certificate of each verified chain must be a configured anchor, leaf validity is judged at the authoritative clock, the CRL must be signature-verified, structurally valid and fresh before membership, and no serial in the presented chain may appear in the CRL; verdicts precede decode and scope enforcement before any ingest side effect
security_review.storage: No parallel storage authority; the guard imports only the standard library and internal/contracts and the unchanged C05 adapter remains the single durability boundary
security_review.transport: TLS 1.3 only, RequireAndVerifyClientCert, local anchors as the only ClientCAs pool, session tickets disabled and VerifyConnection wired to the same authoritative verdict on every connection including resumes; revocation is a locally delivered signed CRL rechecked against the clock on every verdict with fail-closed staleness; focused trace shows loopback-only connect() syscalls
security_review.dependencies: Standard library only; locked dependencies, Go toolchain pin and protected files unchanged

failed_attempts.phase: First guard version required HandshakeComplete in Verify
failed_attempts.note: TLS 1.3 invokes the server-side VerifyConnection after processing the client certificate, before the handshake completes, so the verdict never saw HandshakeComplete=true. Resolution: the verdict is keyed on the presented certificates and trust state; recorded in the committed implementation comments. No log was captured because this failure occurred during interactive development before evidence collection.
failed_attempts.resolution: Verify now accepts VerifyConnection handshake states; the tests pass with the committed implementation.

failed_attempts.phase: Negative dial assertions expected client-side handshake failure
failed_attempts.note: In TLS 1.3 the client handshake finishes before the server examines the client certificate, so a later server-side rejection cannot fail the dial. Resolution: the negative tests treat the listener verdict plus unchanged durable state as the authority. No log was captured; the committed tests encode this semantics.
failed_attempts.resolution: Tests now await listener-side typed failures with zero receipts and an unchanged manifest.

observed_limitations: Remote GitHub Actions execution unverified; no push/publication.
Local identity guard only: no HTTP/UI ingest endpoint, certificate issuance, OCSP or owner/tenant model; the real ingest endpoint belongs to C16 and rotation to C24.
Revocation depends on a trusted local clock and a locally delivered CRL; hostile host-clock rollback and network revocation transports are outside this scope.
Loopback tracing of the focused mTLS binary does not certify C13 decoy isolation, physical power-loss recovery or the full domain workflow.
No C30 usability or C40 release claim.
rollback_or_recovery_observation: The guard is process-local state with no durable writes: redeploying a stale or invalid configuration fails closed at construction and cannot poison storage. Already-ingested events and prior receipts stay valid under the unchanged C05 authority; a later revocation is enforced by configuration-only change on the next connection.

verification_notes: Validation ran against the final mTLS source, fixtures, guards and documentation. The diff check and clean-clone runs used isolated temporary candidate snapshots: no branch, remote ref or delivery commit moved during candidate verification. TLS 1.3 invokes the server-side VerifyConnection between client-certificate processing and handshake completion, so typed verdicts are evaluated on captured real ConnectionState values while transport denials are asserted from the listener outcome, receipts and unchanged manifest. Existing C07 event bytes are reused unchanged through the real sensor/store pipeline. clean_snapshot records the separate temporary source-proof object; metadata edits made after candidate verification only publish these evidence fields, matching the recorded C08 precedent.
